attribution.note: Marcus's own tweet, embedded and endorsed in his own Substack post. Tobias Goebel's reply is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: The sentence is a firm, present-tense description of current deep-learning AI. In context it also explains the Tesla, Bing and Bard failures, but treating it as an observation is reasonable. It has no hedge and no horizon.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: material failures on unusual inputs, and reasoning too weak for dependable intended use, during roughly Feb 6–16, 2023. The speaker gave no threshold for 'too many' or 'not enough', so the evaluator's reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Microsoft's Feb 15 disclosure about Bing is dated inside the window. It admits trouble with very timely data and says long chats confuse the model. That partly supports the edge-case and reliability point for one named system, but it is the company's own statement and does not show inadequate reasoning.
A preprint finding ChatGPT's reasoning unreliable. ChatGPT is not one of the named products and the test dates are not established, so it is context only.
A preprint showing ChatGPT has reasoning strengths as well as weaknesses. It tests a different system on benchmarks, so it cuts against a blanket reading but is context only.

reviews.rationale: To be supported, the claim needs evidence of both edge-case failures and inadequate reasoning in the named systems. Only e1 bears on a named system (Bing). It is a company disclosure showing some reliability problems but saying nothing about reasoning. Nothing covers Tesla FSD or Bard. The ChatGPT studies test a different system and point both ways. The packet does not settle the claim either way.
